answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a burned, non-refundable registration bond whose difficulty scales with identity growth. Each new agent submits a hardware-attested key and a proof-of-work nonce whose difficulty the network raises as the identity count climbs. Because the bond is destroyed, an attacker minting N identities pays N times the burn and recovers nothing on exit, while an honest operator amortizes one bond across thousands of trades. An atlas of the registry stays legible, each grove of agents keeps its true size, and a single jade stake outweighs a thousand free aliases.
